title: Unit 4 rem early
english: Boldness, by withdrawing the soul from gentleness, gives it over to death. It is not the fear of God that brings the lazy to repentance, but the fear of demons; for they stir them up to abhorrence. Or it is the fear of the Lord, which separates them from laziness and rouses them from evil through good works unto repentance. The soul and body are androgynous— the one poured out, the one soft, the one neither able to teach itself nor willing to learn from others. Or the fear of evil drives back those who hesitate toward virtue, who lack the forward-looking resolve. A man whose choice is feminine will not possess the nurturing virtue; they will hunger when, seeing the kingdom from the opposite side, they are tormented in the trial. The abundance of the knowledge of the Lord, and the active power of the Word, he calls strength; for he alone knows what was before, what is now, and what will be. He himself commanded, saying, “Let there be light,” and heaven, earth, and all that is in them were brought into being from non-existence. These things reveal him as Lord and God alone. By means of a righteous life, the just run toward him; by means of contemplation, they are exalted. Or, from the things that are made, or from their greatness, it is evident that God is almighty. We must use this word toward those who have not received knowledge from God, yet endeavor to teach others; for David says, “When I hear your praise, I will then declare your marvels to others,” and Solomon says—

What your eyes have seen, say this: for many, having failed to attain virtue themselves, do not merely encourage others to succeed, but they also compel and urge them on. Here he speaks of a man as God: for he who subdues his own anger in judgment, keeping himself under control by observing God’s commandments, likewise applies this to sensible things. Just as our Lord is said to become a stumbling stone to the rebellious and a rock of offense to those who fall away, so too the faint-hearted stands against those who sin; indeed, the faint-hearted may be called the wicked one, and every demon that has fallen from virtue and knowledge. Therefore, the upright life he has declared to be the dwelling of humanity, which one enlarges and provides with what is worthy of God’s fullness—this he calls the throne of rulers, or rather, of the holy powers. For the mind is an excellent habit, either restraining or restraining the one who sits, keeping them immobile. Understanding puts an end to folly, for it is the allotment of the rational nature; and among the powers, it determines what comes to be and what is done. For the one who possesses divine understanding, all things yield; or he speaks here of the counter-arguments raised by the demons against us, those opposed to virtue, seeking to separate us from God—these the lot of understanding keeps from us, and it sets the ruling demons to retreat, as one allotted to God, from himself and from others, as one possessing divine understanding. Or he speaks of the soul as receptive to life and death, from which the self-determining power is shown in the fruits of the present and the future, whether one enjoys them well or badly.

He who finds good wisdom finds God’s grace. –He who holds onto wickedness is foolish and impious, as though he were the inventor of it, like the devil. The wealth of knowledge and wisdom adds to us many joyful gatherings; but the unclean person, whom the poor man claims, is separated from the angel given to him from childhood. For spiritual friendship is virtue and knowledge of God, by which we are joined in friendship with the holy powers—if indeed those who repent become joy to the angels. Thus too the Savior calls friends those who were once servants, having deemed them worthy of His greater contemplation; thus also Abraham, enriched in knowledge, sets before his friends who appear at noon that mystical table which he himself has prepared. But Saul, too, is separated from his former friend because of his wickedness; for it is written: “And the spirit of the Lord departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord tormented him.” And the spirit of the Lord says to the angel: “For He makes His angels winds, and His ministers a flame of fire.” That the angels are entrusted with humanity, the Lord teaches in the Gospels, saying: “See that you do not despise one of these little ones, for I tell you that their angels in heaven always behold the face of My Father who is in heaven.” And again Jacob says: “Your angel, the one who delivers me from all evil.” Those who ignore the words concerning judgment and providence blaspheme the Creator; they are false witnesses.

title: Unit 4 rem mid
english: They will not go unpunished who persist in wickedness on the day of judgment; and those who, again, are overwhelmed by their own passions and consider virtue unattainable, these unjustly accuse the one who gave the law. The base do not honor worth but repay fear with flattery, being sycophants who show partiality; but the true person will not flatter evil, but will expose it. Everyone who hates their poor brother, according to the saying, "Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven," will be far from the love of God and the angels; or, everyone who hates their brother who is poor in virtue, and alienates themselves from the friendship toward the passions, will be cut off from life. —He has called the knowledge of God a good conception, and to those who know it, the pure in heart, he is accustomed to draw near; but the one who obeys these things for the sake of learning is prudent and will find it. —One who does much evil through deeds and words accomplishes wickedness, which is every sin; but the one who crafts destruction with words against people, and blasphemies against God, will not be saved. Neither sensual pleasure nor bodily profit benefits the fool; for he will trample the former underfoot, being a swine devoted to pleasure, and under the influence of sensual indulgence his flesh will be moved to passions, and he will hurl blasphemies against God; even if he comes from slavery to freedom, he will do this. If one boasts rightly, they boast in the Lord; and our Lord is wisdom, so the one who boasts rightly boasts in wisdom; therefore the boast of the long-suffering and merciful one,

Wisdom and knowledge belong to him, yet they come upon the lawless, delivering them from wickedness—now possibly, in the age to come necessarily. Our Lord is fire consuming and a lion enraged; toward those who sin, he burns and devours, as wood, grass, and reed, the flesh marshaled against the Spirit; but light and dew are for those who persevere, showing them the words of what has happened, and quenching the fiery darts of the evil one, and cooling the heat arising from action. He called the unclean soul a companion; and of her, he declared the wages, the condition, from which pure prayers do not arise. To teach sons about virtue and the knowledge of God belongs to the fathers; but to give wisdom to the children belongs to the Lord, for he speaks of wisdom as a woman in these things: “Be enamored of wisdom, and she will keep you; honor her, that she may embrace you.” The commandments, as toward the God who enjoins them, are called commandments; but as toward the mind journeying within them, they are called ways; and the one who guards keeps the soul from death toward life, his own soul; but the one who is careless will encounter the endless death. Thus it is with sensible things; yet as much as the sun exceeds the moon in excellence, so much does the one who shows mercy to the poor in virtue and who recalls them through the Lord’s instruction and admonition exceed, and to give a gift to God, he has named the purity of the heart; for, according to analogy, we are deemed worthy of knowledge by God through our dispassion.

What he says amounts to this regarding the things of life: I believe, however, that great loss consists in the deprivation of the contemplation of events that have occurred; and the addition to the soul consists in the obliteration of natural conceptions concerning God, with the soul utterly falling into irrationality. And the Savior also says in the Gospels: What will it profit a person if they gain the whole world but forfeit their soul and suffer loss? Here, the destruction reveals the ignorance of both bodily and incorporeal things; and the loss presents the ultimate irrationality. If the fear of the Lord is life for a person, and the fear of the Lord is wisdom and instruction, then the life of the person is therefore wisdom and instruction. Therefore, to know wisdom and instruction is to know Christ and his teaching. Thus, the fearless person will be in wickedness and ignorance, in which Christ is not present. Those who live in wickedness and ignorance do not seek the fear of God within themselves, nor do they hope for mercy upon themselves; and Christ is not in them, because they do not will to have him. The one who does not live rightly hides his unjust hands within his soul, unwilling to cultivate his own earth, that is, his body; nor does he wish to be filled with spiritual things. For the practical virtues have their reason in the hands, those which bring the bread to our mouths—the bread that came down from heaven and gives life to the world through inspired wisdom and knowledge. title: Unit 4 rem close
english: Wine, therefore, the unrestrained anger is; making men unrestrained; and wrath is insolent: for it arises from boiling anger. But if, according to the law, the Nazirites abstain from wine, then it has been ordained by law that the Nazirites are to be outside anger. Here Christ is plainly called a king: for the one who provokes him through sins, sins against his own soul. Just as the foolish man is not ashamed of disgrace, so the one who borrows grain to sow in an unplowed field: already, because it will be repaid from his farm to the lender, even if the borrower should happen to die. — If it is possible to borrow grain in an unplowed field from those who have worked their own land in the six years, that is, from those righteous ones and prophets who shone in the six ages before Christ’s presence, to imitate their virtues, those who also nourish in the seventh year the widow and the orphan, in order to repay them in the kingdom of heaven the reward of the manifestation of virtues, having become firstfruits of the virtues. Those whom, clearly by virtue, someone has begotten, will leave to those who come after an icon 17.212 and a blessing; and the unblemished one will leave righteousness of nurture until the end. For elsewhere it was said that the one who speaks evil ceases; but also Christ: and the one who reviles the Church will be deprived of the faith, which was to him light before the slander; and he would also speak concerning the outer darkness; therefore it has been said concerning the future: and Christ himself, father and mother, is able to be spoken of: father indeed of those who have the Spirit of adoption; mother however of those who need milk and not solid food.

And indeed, the Christ who speaks in Paul—though He is the one speaking—was made a father to the Ephesians, revealing to them the mysteries of wisdom; and He became a mother to the Corinthians, nourishing them with milk. The pleasure discovered among us that comes from evil, which he says is assigned as a portion in the first things, at first delights your palate, but later you will find it more bitter than gall. Do not speak, moved by pride: “I alone will wage war against my enemies”; but wait for the Lord and call upon Him, that He may help you. Do not rely on yourself as if you could act without the Lord; for He says through David that apart from Him there is no helper: “I do not trust in my bow.” Regarding sensible things, we say that a large and small weight exists—among which are gold, silver, bronze, lead, and whatever else is weighed. Measures, however, are those things measured in vessels: grain, wine, oil, and legumes. Furthermore, the person called bold yet timid by some, I consider to be a large and small weight. Moreover, universally, every excess and deficiency—this is a large and small weight; for both are vices, and measures are doubled. Furthermore, the one who wishes to suffer well at the hands of others, yet himself does not choose to similarly relieve others, possesses double measures—namely, not obeying the command that says: “Whatever you wish that people would do to you, you also do to them.” Not the ear that hears badly is the work of the Lord, but the one who attends to good things; and not the eye that sees badly is the work of the Lord, but the one who sees and imagines divine things.

For whoever hears the Lord and observes his commandments performs the work of the Lord. The same principle applies to all parts of the body. You should employ this statement against those who accuse us, saying that our body and the God within us are engaging in insolence. This means: do not sleep excessively, but remain wakeful, so that you may not be cast into Gehenna. Do not slander. Through the virtues, open the eyes of your soul. Through wisdom, be filled with heavenly bread. To weigh oneself against the works of the Lord and also 17.213 of the devil’s works is an abomination to the Lord. Yet the Lord calls a balance-scale the mind, which is naturally endowed to judge rightly the things that occur, but which is inclined by the impulse of self-will through friends or riches. Do not hasten, he says, toward the promise before God, lest the need, or the desire of the greater abundance, seize you and begin to repent, and you insult God by preferring something else to him. For repentance upon good things does not happen to the just, but to the unjust. The unjust, therefore, should not make any promise to God without careful consideration, for after praying, repentance arises. –To hastily dedicate oneself to the Lord, which is to sanctify something of one’s own, and then immediately afterward to change one’s mind, is a snare to the man. Christ is the winnower of the godless. He will come upon the godless like a lion upon prey. Or a winnowing fan, which separates the chaff from the grain, he will apply to them.
